title: AI-MED Project Definition
description: Defines a project: cases + frontend + optional Kobo form + tabs + feature flags + deployment config. Validated on every build by tools/validate-projects.ts, so every field a project.json may carry must be declared here (additionalProperties is false).

name.description: Project slug: lowercase letters, digits and underscores. Must equal the directory name under projects/, the VITE_PROJECT build value and the X-Project header. URLs use the hyphenated form (haivn_eip is served at /haivn-eip/).

systemPrompt.description: Path to system prompt file (relative to repo root)

key.description: Vignette identifier: the same characters and length the frontend accepts in ?vignette= (readVignetteParam in talk-paper.ts). Readable names, hyphen-stripped UUIDs, or <deck>--<slide-id> for the decks project

file.description: Path to vignette content file (relative to repo root)

profileId.description: Demographic profile ID from the template's profiles.json. Null if hand-written.

kobo.description: Assessment form. Required unless the project is formless.

formUid.description: Deployed Kobo form UID (null until deployed)

formUrl.description: Deployed Kobo form URL (null until deployed)

languages.description: ISO 639-1 language codes supported by this project; each must have a block in languages.json

tabs.description: Right-panel tab structure. Declaring one id twice, once 'pdf' and once 'document', makes a single tab with a Text/PDF switcher.

label.description: Localized tab label, keyed by language code

contentFile.description: Repo-relative content path, or a map of language code to path

showForVignetteKeys.description: Tab is visible only when the selected vignette key is in this list; omit to show on every vignette

docRefs.description: Linkify numbered document references in chat answers into the named document tab

app.description: Which application the project is: the clinical simulator (default) or document chat. talk implies formless, enableFeedback:false, skipWelcome and enableFollowups, and needs no kobo block; explicit flags are still accepted and win over the implied ones. Without app, formless:true means talk, as before

groundingFile.description: Repo-relative path to the corpus grounding file appended to the prompt after the document (a compact index of the corpus the project answers from)

groundingSets.description: Document sets grounded on their own file, each the part of a vignette key before "--" (a deck's slides are <deck>--<slide>). A turn whose current document is in a listed set is grounded on projects/<slug>/grounding/<set>.md (the checkout, then the private store) instead of groundingFile; any other turn, or a set whose file is in neither place, uses groundingFile. One grounding per turn: the earlier document of a followHost turn adds none of its own. Each set must be some vignette's document set, and grounding/ may hold only these files (tools/validate-projects.ts); a private (gitignored) set file reaches a deployment through tools/push-content.ts, which refuses to push when a listed set's file is neither in the checkout nor deployed. See packages/chat-core/CLAUDE.md

enableFeedback.description: Real-time grading feedback after form submission

enableFollowups.description: Inline AI-suggested follow-up question chips above the chat input

formless.description: Pure Q&A advisor: no Kobo form tab, no grading

skipWelcome.description: Open straight into the chat, skipping the welcome/consent screen

dragDropAllocation.description: Management project: drag-and-drop worker allocation panel

requireKnownVignette.description: Refuse a deep link (?vignette=) naming no vignette or an unknown one, instead of opening the first vignette: /api/vignettes?vignette=<key> answers 404 and the page says so

followHost.description: Talk page only: the page that frames the chat says which document is current (postMessage host:document), and one conversation runs across documents. Implied by nothing; requires app "talk" and embedOrigins (tools/validate-projects.ts). See packages/chat-core/CLAUDE.md, "Following a host page"

embedOrigins.description: followHost only: the origins (scheme://host[:port], no path, no trailing slash) whose host:document messages the talk page obeys; a message from any other origin, or from any window but the page's parent, is ignored. The API server, which serves the talk page, also lets only these origins (and its own) frame it: Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors 'self' <origins> (packages/api/src/talk/pages.ts)

urlAliases.description: Talk page only: former URL slugs of this project's page; the API server answers /<alias>/<rest> with a 301 to /<url-slug>/<rest>. Requires app "talk", and may not be another project's URL slug or alias (tools/validate-projects.ts)

historyTokens.description: followHost only: the most conversation history, in estimated tokens (characters / 4), one turn sends the model; the oldest turns are dropped first and the log keeps everything. Default 24000

days.description: How long after the last turn a saved conversation is brought back; older ones are discarded

rememberConversation.description: Talk page only: the reader's browser keeps the conversation (the visible thread and its session token, in localStorage, nothing on the server), so reloading or reopening the page brings it back; a New conversation control in the header starts afresh. One saved thread per project and document set (the key before "--"). Requires app "talk" (tools/validate-projects.ts). See packages/frontend-chat/CLAUDE.md, "Remembering the conversation"

requireAccessCode.description: Gate the project behind an access code from the access_code project setting or ACCESS_CODE_<SLUG>; fails closed when none is configured. Also withholds vignetteInfo from /api/languages until the code is given

logConversations.description: Write every chat turn to the global qa_log table (the durable store for formless advisors)

chatModel.description: Chat model override; the keys of CHAT_MODEL_PRICES in packages/chat-core/src/chat/usage.ts (usage.test.ts checks this enum against them)

readingsIndex.description: Repo-relative path to a SQLite readings corpus (FTS5 + optional embeddings) built by tools/build-*-corpus.py; in production the READINGS_INDEX_<SLUG> env var points at the uploaded copy on the Railway volume

readingsQueryLanguage.description: Language the corpus is written in, named in English; queries are restated into it before retrieval, except in a session already in it (the session language is matched through languages.json, so "Tiếng Việt" matches "Vietnamese")

retrievalScope.description: What a search_readings call may return: the whole readings corpus (corpus, the default) or only the passages of the document the turn is about (document; the vignette key must be the index's document id). Enforced by the server, so the model cannot widen it

searchFirst.description: Require a search_readings call on the first completion of every turn (tool_choice required on hop 0 only); later hops choose freely. Default false

talkManifest.description: Repo-relative path to a JSON manifest {"papers": [{"doi", "title", "vignette"}]} served publicly at GET /api/talk-manifest/<slug> for external 'Talk to this paper' buttons. Declaring it puts the project behind the public_chat kill switch (default off): when off the manifest is empty and /api/chat, /api/tts, /api/realtime/session and /api/grade-session return 503 code public_chat_disabled.

talkPublicUrl.description: Public front door for a talkManifest project: a URL template on the author's own site, e.g. https://www.benjaminbdaniels.com/publications/#talk-doi-{slug}. {slug} is the DOI lower-cased with every run outside [a-z0-9] replaced by '-' and trimmed (orcid-display's slugForWork); {doi} is the URL-encoded DOI. Opened top-level (not in an iframe), the frontend redirects there: filled for the paper ?paper=/?vignette= names, else with the fragment stripped. The talk manifest route adds each paper's filled publicUrl.

tablePrefix.description: Database table prefix for multi-tenancy; conventionally equal to name

allOf.$comment: A project needs at least one vignette, unless it sets requireKnownVignette: such a project opens only the vignette a deep link names and refuses any other, so it may exist before its content is synced. Every other project would open its first vignette, and must have one.
